newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain shipments to Pacific port near target.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain shipments to Pacific port near target.

text.p: Grain and oilseed deliveries to Canada's Pacific ports improved in the past week ended Sunday to reach near target, rail and grain officials said.
A total of 2,972 hopper cars were unloaded in Vancouver, or 99 percent of the 3,000 railcar target, in the week ended February 23, Canadian Wheat Board spokeswoman Rhea Yates said.
That compared to 2,484 railcar unloads the week February 16 and 1,994 the week ended February 9, Yates said.
"I'd say the improvement is a combination of our better weather, the premium is having an effect," Canadian National Railway Co spokesman Jim Feeny said.
Forty eight ships waited to load on Canada's Pacific coast on Friday. One ship had been berthed for 50 days.
Demurrage fees average about C$10,000 a ship each day and the CWB already faces more than C$15 million in fines as well as a one-month backlog in Asian grain shipments.
Along with warmer weather and transportation premiums, terminals in Vancouver handled weekend unloads, Feeny added.
CN doubled its freight rebates from February 9 to March 6.

Blocks of 25 to 49 hopper cars that can be loaded with grains and oilseeds in one location for the same destination usually qualify for a C$0.75 a tonne discount but CN raised the premium to C$1.50 from February 9 to March 6, Feeny said.

Discounts were raised to C$4 a tonne from the normal C$2 on blocks of 50 to 95 hopper cars and discounts on blocks of more than 95 hopper cars were increased to C$6 until March 6 from the usual C$3 a tonne rebate.
Canadian Pacific Ltd unit CP Rail System also offered shipping premiums, CP spokesman Steve Morris said.
"We're just about back to normal," Morris added.
Hopper car unloads in Prince Rupert reached 1,105, or 85 percent of the 1,300 target last week. Thunder Bay unloads reached 499, exceeding the target of 490, CWB's Yates said.
